A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MME-RealWorld and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-B. Their content can be reliably matched despite section removal and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 28 MLLMs on English and Chinese perception and reasoning tasks, alongside error analyses and detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark evaluations and analyses, adds Qwen2-VL results, and revises several reported scores.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, manual annotation workflow, question format, and answer-matching procedure remain unchanged. Qwen2-VL is an additional evaluated comparator, not a proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same English and Chinese benchmarks across OCR, remote sensing, diagrams and tables, monitoring, and autonomous driving. Appendix A retains the same data sources, task definitions, and examples.

E2.justification: Qwen2-VL is added to all four main comparisons in Tables 3-6 and to Figure 2, supplementing the retained 28 models. The appendix comparisons in Tables 7-12 retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: Table 1's prompting, rule-based scoring, Avg and Avg-C metrics, and evaluation sample counts remain unchanged. The numerical revisions are not accompanied by reported changes to splits, preprocessing, budgets, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: The answer-E frequency analysis, incorrect-choice distributions, computational-efficiency comparison, and Appendix B analyses are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Changes to accuracy values do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 6 replaces the Chinese reasoning scores for all 28 retained models: InternVL-2's Avg changes from 44.12 to 46.65, Claude's from 38.74 to 44.31, and Gemini's from 15.96 to 11.14. Table 5 changes InternVL-2's Chinese perception Avg from 59.70 to 57.97. Qwen2-VL adds results throughout Tables 3-6, leading English perception at 58.96. Figure 2 also revises numerous existing scores, including InternVL-2's English score from 50.3 to 53.5.

T1.justification: The dataset notation and mathematical definitions of Avg and Avg-C are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions, proofs, or additional formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a large, fully human-annotated, high-resolution benchmark, a dedicated Chinese benchmark, and overall model accuracy below 60%. Updating the evaluated-model count from 28 to 29 extends supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 Section 3.2 extends the interpretation of strong Chinese performance from InternVL-2 to Qwen2-VL, attributing both to Chinese-specific optimization. Explanations involving resolution, conservative responses, dynamic-scene difficulties, and applicability limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Qwen2-VL repository footnote and identifies its 7B backbone in the result tables. Benchmark code/data access statements, annotation details, prompts, and computational-cost information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v3 removes v1's entire Related Work section, including dedicated discussions of multimodal benchmarks, MLLM development, and high-resolution architectures. This substantially reduces explicit research positioning, although the bibliography and introductory benchmark comparisons remain.

P1.justification: The structural edit removes Related Work and renumbers subsequent sections and cross-references. Perception findings become bullets and several model-related passages are edited, but most remaining prose and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves earlier and gains a leaderboard entry; Tables 3-6 gain Qwen2-VL rows, and Table 2 reorders benchmarks. Displays reflow within the existing design, while appendix tables and illustrations retain their layouts.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical reporting: v1 Table 6 repeats Table 4's numerical rows under different model names, whereas v3's retained-model Chinese reasoning averages largely agree with their domain scores and sample counts. Qwen2-VL adds useful comparison evidence. These gains are tempered by removal of related-work discussion and unresolved inconsistencies: Qwen2-VL's Table 6 Avg is 46.46, although its displayed domain scores and sample counts imply approximately 50.07.
